newsitem.title: MALTA: Drop in electronics thwarts Malta exports growth.
newsitem.headline: Drop in electronics thwarts Malta exports growth.

text.p: Growth in most categories of domestic exports by Malta during the first nine months of last year was not enough to match a decline in exports in the machinery and transport equipment sector, government figures showed on Monday.

Domestic exports declined to 416.7 million Maltese pounds ($1,125 million) between January and September 1996 from 446.1 million pounds in the same period of the previous year, official figures showed.
The machinery and transport equipment category accounts for 62 per cent of domestic exports thanks to the Malta plant of the Franco-Italian SGS-Thomson electronics group.
Exports in this category declined by 42 million pounds to 258.5 million pounds in the first three quarters of 1996 after the firm completed work on a major sub-contract.
The sector was also influenced by fluctuations in the international price of semi-conductors and related products, the figures from an official economic survey report showed.
The report said exports were down by 1.5 million pounds to 10.7 million pounds in the toys and games category.
Exports were up by an aggregate 14.5 million pounds in food, beverages and tobacco, chemicals, semi-manufactures, clothing, printed matter sector, scientific instruments and furniture.
The drop in exports of electronic machinery reduced the European Union share of Maltese exports to 61 percent from 74.2 percent in the first three quarters of 1995.
Italy remained Malta's biggest trading partner, but at 71.5 million pounds, less than half that recorded in the first nine months of 1995, because of the drop in electronics sales, the report said.
Sales to Asia doubled to reach 80.1 million pounds and 17.5 percent of total Maltese exports.

To diversify markets, Maltese firms have entered into sub-contracting agreements with Asian firms. This has resulted in an increase in the export of key products such as electronic machinery to markets like Singapore, the report said.
Exports to the US rose by 25.5 percent to 59.6 million pounds, with increases in rubber, plastics, jewellery and electrical equipment. (1$ = 36 cents)
